title: PPE Non-compliance — Researcher Working Without Lab Coat and Gloves
description: A visiting scholar was observed working with organic solvents (dichloromethane and acetone) wearing only jeans and a t-shirt — no lab coat and no gloves. The visitor was unaware that the laboratory's PPE policy applied to visiting researchers. When confronted by a lab manager, the researcher stated they were 'only making a quick observation' and had not intended to handle chemicals. However, they were observed actively pipetting with bare hands.
violations_identified: Failure to wear lab coat in the laboratory (SOP-LAB-001 Section 1.1)
Failure to wear gloves when handling chemical solvents (SOP-LAB-001 Section 1.1)
Working with organic solvents without appropriate skin protection (SOP-CHEM-002 Section 1.2)
root_cause: Laboratory induction process did not cover visiting researchers. No PPE requirement communicated at laboratory entry point. Lab coat and gloves not provided or made accessible to visitors.
corrective_actions_taken: Visitor induction protocol created: all visitors sign safety acknowledgement before entry
PPE station established at laboratory entrance with spare lab coats and gloves for visitors
Clear 'PPE REQUIRED BEYOND THIS POINT' signage installed at lab entrance
Lab manager checklist includes verifying visitor PPE compliance at start of visit
outcome: No injuries. Visitor was escorted out until PPE could be obtained. Incident reported to department safety committee.
lessons_learned: PPE compliance policies must extend to ALL persons entering the lab, including visitors. Physical provision of PPE at entry points reduces barriers to compliance.
content: Incident INC-2024-033: Visiting scholar working with DCM and acetone with no lab coat and no gloves. PPE policy not communicated to visitors. Active chemical handling observed without protection. Root cause: no visitor induction, no PPE at entry. Corrective actions: visitor protocol, PPE station at entrance, signage, manager checklist.
